title: Transported scalar and sections-limit data
statement: For a coefficient reduction R and finite tensor normalization hF, there is a nonempty data package consisting of scalar coherence, derived tower-section evaluation isomorphisms, and the prescribed total-limit comparison, before the resolution and projection equations.

source.place: Tags 03CZ, 079P, 08JA, 0D6E and 0941; extracted data stage of the normalized coefficient-sections construction.

proof.text: Identify Hom from the module unit with compatible sections by evaluating at one and the universal property of the presheaf limit. This additive natural isomorphism identifies Coyoneda sections with the limit model of sections. For restriction of scalars, the underlying presheaf is unchanged; conjugating the identity by these isomorphisms gives the ordinary scalar comparison. Its value at one is unchanged, and linearity gives the required scalar formula.

Transport restriction-of-scalars sections acyclicity along the ordinary section isomorphism. Resolve a restricted K-injective complex by a K-injective complex; acyclicity and naturality of the derived unit show that the completed-sections unit on the restricted complex is invertible. Record the actual sections functors and site comparison units as right-derived pairs. The composite of exact restriction and the completed-sections pair is then a right derivation. Uniqueness of right derivation applied to the ordinary scalar isomorphism gives the scalar comparison and its required unit equation directly in the recorded model.

Instantiate the generic tower comparison with the actual right-derived sections functors and their canonical units. Combine its evaluation isomorphism with the existing restricted-evaluation isomorphism and the scalar comparison to obtain each systemSectionsEvaluation field.

Inverse limit preserves K-injective complexes because its constant left adjoint is exact. The proved tower-image acyclicity lemma makes derived abelian inverse limit after derived tower sections a right derivation of the other ordinary composite. Sections preserve limits, so the ordinary composites are naturally isomorphic. Uniqueness of right derivation gives the total-limit comparison. Whisker it with exact coefficient-sequence restriction and assemble the three fields.

proof_origin.place: Derived restriction and sections comparisons, Tags 079P, 0941 and 0D6E; direct application to the prescribed coefficient functors using the proved generic comparison helpers.
